items.name: S&P 500 (VFV + SPY)
items.street: Strategists are split: earnings are still growing, but the market is leaning on a handful of AI names while yields and oil stay high.
items.take: Crowd mood on the S&P 500 is about as gloomy as it gets, while the index itself has barely pulled back. Your VFV and SPY move together, so this is the sentiment that matters most for you.

bears: Capex of $195–205B this year has pushed free cash flow negative
Debt and equity raising to fund AI build-out
Chart broke support; some traders are calling for $250 if capex rises again
bulls: Google Cloud grew 82% last quarter with a $514B backlog
TPU chips are seen as a $100B+ opportunity and a challenge to Nvidia
Stock looks oversold (RSI near 30) at about 24x forward earnings
items.name: Alphabet
items.street: Strong Buy from 62 analysts; average target about $421–431, roughly a third above Friday's $317 close. Q3 consensus: revenue about $127.5B (+25%), EPS about $3.
items.take: The crowd is divided into two camps: a Cloud blowout sends it higher, a capex hike sends it lower. Your call is about $13 below its $330 strike, so the Oct 28 reaction matters a lot for its value.

bears: About $220B of capex this year weighs on free cash flow
Reports of GPUs sitting idle in warehouses feed bubble talk
Soft retail guidance and a disclosed founder share sale
bulls: AWS growth has sped up five quarters in a row, to 36.7% last quarter
AWS capacity is reported sold out through 2026
Stock is about 13% off its August high at about 24x next year's earnings
items.name: Amazon
items.street: Strong Buy from 60 analysts; average target about $331, about a third above Friday's $248 close. The number everyone is watching is AWS growth (30–35% expected).
items.take: Retail traders are more upbeat on Amazon than on Alphabet going into earnings. Your call is about $12 below its $260 strike; AWS growth vs. the 30–35% range is the swing factor.

mood.summary: Investors are nervous. The Fear & Greed index has sat in Extreme Fear for two weeks, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 9 points, well below the long-run norm. The S&P 500 fell for a second week and is about 2.5% off its Oct 6 record, while the Nasdaq is about 6% off after its worst day since June on Oct 22. Worries centre on AI spending, oil above $110 on Middle East tensions, and a possible Fed hike in December. Very fearful readings have often come before rebounds, but they don't say when.

items.name: ServiceNow
items.about: Sells cloud workflow-automation software to large enterprises.
items.why: Shares closed at $109.83, down about 27% from $150.13, on 68M shares, and slipped a little more after hours. The posts describing the drop cite no specific news, so the cause is unconfirmed; it came on a day when other big tech names such as Amazon, Alphabet and Intel also fell sharply.

items.name: Amazon.com
items.about: Operates the Amazon online marketplace, AWS cloud computing and advertising businesses.
items.why: Amazon fell 4.2% to $243.80 in the regular session ahead of its Q3 report after the close, then dropped roughly 10% more in after-hours trading to about $225-228. Posts say the reaction reflects worry about consumer demand; the report details weren't confirmed here.

items.name: Intel
items.about: Designs and manufactures CPUs and runs a chip foundry business.
items.why: Intel slid 3.7% to $91.98 before reporting, then fell about 25% after hours to roughly $72. Posts citing the release say Q3 EPS was $0.52 vs $0.41 expected on $16.51B revenue vs $16.56B expected, with Q4 revenue guided to $15-16B and non-GAAP EPS to about $0.25; posts also note data center and AI revenue up 78% from a year earlier and a completed $23B equity offering.

items.name: Iovance Biotherapeutics
items.about: Biotech company that makes cell therapies for solid tumors, including lung cancer and melanoma.
items.why: The stock plunged about 35% to $9.57 on 52M shares, its heaviest volume in weeks. Posts say a clinical data update drove it, noting a 24.6% response rate in second-line lung cancer versus higher rates in biomarker-selected subgroups; that detail comes from posts and is unconfirmed.

items.name: Sandisk
items.about: Makes flash memory and solid-state storage, increasingly for data centers.
items.why: Sandisk fell 5.2% to $1,331.52 into its fiscal Q1 report and lost about 9% more after hours. Posts citing the release say adjusted EPS was $49.51 vs about $46.67 expected, revenue $11.03B vs $10.64B, Q2 revenue guided to $12.2-12.6B, and an 8-for-1 stock split was announced.

items.name: Reddit
items.about: Runs the Reddit community discussion platform, earning mainly from advertising and data licensing.
items.why: Reddit closed down 3.3% at $130.26 and fell about 14.6% more after hours to near $115. The posts give no company-specific news; the move coincided with a wider sell-off in large tech and AI-linked names, so the cause is unconfirmed.

items.name: Alphabet (Class A)
items.about: Parent of Google Search, YouTube, Google Cloud and Waymo.
items.why: Alphabet closed at $283.31, down 12.8% from $324.89, after its Q3 results. Posts link to analyst notes: Goldman Sachs trimmed its target to $385 from $435 and MoffettNathanson to $345 from $370, both keeping Buy ratings.

items.name: Marvell Technology
items.about: Designs data-center networking, custom AI silicon and storage chips.
items.why: Marvell dropped 13.3% to $218.30 and slipped further after hours, part of a broad sell-off in AI-linked chip and data-center names. A post tracking options flow noted about $13.9M in Nov 20 $220 puts; no company-specific news was cited.

items.name: Alphabet (Class C)
items.about: Non-voting share class of Alphabet, the parent of Google, YouTube and Google Cloud.
items.why: The Class C shares fell 12.5% to $281.63 after Alphabet's Q3 results, moving in line with Class A. Posts cite Goldman Sachs and MoffettNathanson cutting price targets while keeping Buy ratings.

items.name: Teladoc Health
items.about: Provides virtual healthcare and telehealth services.
items.why: Teladoc jumped 26.8% to $8.73 on 17M shares, with most of the move coming midday. Posts attribute the move to no specific headline, so the catalyst is unconfirmed; some posts mention short sellers.

items.name: Norwegian Cruise Line
items.about: Operates cruise ships under the Norwegian, Oceania and Regent brands.
items.why: Norwegian rose 13.6% to $18.24 on about 56M shares, well above normal. Posts note the move spread to other cruise lines such as Royal Caribbean and Carnival but cite no specific news, so the catalyst is unconfirmed.

items.name: Omeros
items.about: Biopharma company developing treatments for rare blood and immune disorders.
items.why: Omeros rose 6% to $18.96, closing near its high. Posts say it moved without any announcement and look ahead to upcoming earnings; no catalyst was confirmed.

items.name: SELLAS Life Sciences
items.about: Clinical-stage biotech developing a cancer vaccine candidate for blood cancers.
items.why: SELLAS closed 1.9% lower at $10.18 after an intraday range of $9.87-$11.09. Posts debate trial results and the size of the study's control group; the details are unconfirmed and several posts are promotional.

items.name: Strategy
items.about: Business-software firm that holds a large bitcoin treasury.
items.why: Strategy slipped 2.4% to $141.63 before reporting. Posts citing the release say Q3 EPS was $44.75 vs $8.17 expected, driven by bitcoin gains, while revenue of $125.4M missed the $127.2M estimate; shares were roughly flat after hours.

items.name: Hyperliquid Strategies
items.about: Public company holding the Hyperliquid (HYPE) crypto token as a treasury asset.
items.why: Hyperliquid Strategies gained 23.6% to $12.32 on 53M shares, closing at its high. Posts point to a video in which President Trump mentioned Hyperliquid for the first time at a White House meeting with crypto executives; that link is from posts and unconfirmed.

items.name: Roblox
items.about: Runs the Roblox online platform where users play and build games.
items.why: Roblox slipped 1.9% to $52.26 into its report, then fell about 12% after hours to near $47. Posts mention heavy put buying before earnings; the results themselves weren't confirmed here.

items.name: Twilio
items.about: Provides cloud communications APIs for messaging, voice and customer engagement.
items.why: Twilio fell 4.4% to $242.70 ahead of its Q3 report after the close and dropped about 20% after hours to near $203. A post notes it had beaten EPS estimates in its last eight reports; the new results weren't confirmed here.

items.name: Pinterest
items.about: Runs the Pinterest visual discovery and shopping platform, earning from ads.
items.why: Pinterest fell 4.8% to $19.92 into its Q3 report and slid about 16% after hours to near $17.59. A post summarizing options activity cited heavy put buying, an implied move of about 12%, and consensus of roughly $1.20B revenue and $0.41 EPS.

items.name: Rivian Automotive
items.about: Builds electric trucks, SUVs and delivery vans.
items.why: Rivian closed 1.8% lower at $11.47 and was little changed after hours. Posts citing its Q3 release say revenue was $2.15B (+38% from a year earlier) with a GAAP loss of $0.48 per share, 2026 deliveries guided to 67,000-70,000, and the adjusted EBITDA loss guide narrowed by $100M at the midpoint.

items.name: Crocs
items.about: Sells Crocs clogs and the HEYDUDE casual shoe brand.
items.why: Crocs surged 25% to $149.79, a two-year high, after Q3 results. Posts say EPS was $3.69 on $1.043B revenue, guidance was raised, and HEYDUDE sales improved.
